newsitem.title: UK: CIA says interested in alliances, not sale.
newsitem.headline: CIA says interested in alliances, not sale.

text.p: CIA Group Plc, Europe's second largest independent media buying, planning and research agency, wants to form alliances as part of its growth strategy, but is not interested in selling the company, Chairman Chris Ingram said on Tuesday.

Ingram spoke to Reuters in a phone interview following an announcement on Tuesday by WPP Group Plc that it had agreed to acquire a 14.4 percent stake in CIA of six million shares for a total cash price of 10.2 million stg ($16.7 million). WPP said the shares were being acquired as an investment.

As clients themselves become increasingly global, CIA is moving to meet their needs by expanding into a global network, Ingram said. "Hence us looking at the building of alliances," he told Reuters. "But that does not include selling our business."
Commenting on WPP's purchase, Ingram said, "It wasn't altogether a surprise, but we didn't invite it.
"But as long as it remains an investment, it's not a problem," he added.
CIA's shares rose 14-1/2 pence to 174-1/2 pence in late afternoon trade on the London Stock Exchange. WPP's shares were trading up 5-1/2 pence at 247-1/2p.
WPP, the world's largest advertising and marketing group, declined to comment on its purchase of the CIA stake.
But WPP, which owns some 400 companies including Ogilvy & Mather and J Walter Thompson ad agencies, has made no secret of its interest in the areas of media buying, planning and research.
WPP in its 1996 annual report noted the "spectacular concentrations of monopoly media power" and its effect on media pricing.

"There is a solution to this: the concentration of media buying power to counterbalance the selling points -- not necessarily in an antagonistic way, but by harnessing the constructive opportunities of programming, sponsorship, syndication and barter, and most importantly media research," WPP said in the annual report.
The company stressed that "...increased focus has developed on media buying with the growth of media independents like Carat and CIA..."

Media fragmentation is an increasing concern, meaning that "the need for co-ordination between the creative and media functions will therefore increase and the demand for integrated approaches intensify," WPP said in the annual report.
Media planners and buyers work with advertisers to help allocate advertising budgets between various media.
WPP, which is considering merging the media operations of J Walter Thompson and Ogilvy & Mather, started looking at a purchase of the CIA stake only recently, an industry source said.
One industry source said WPP had not ruled out developing business ventures with CIA further down the road.
CIA's Ingram said that as part of his company's drive to become one of the top six media buyers worldwide it has "made no secret that alliances with major partners could be achieved".
"So we have been talking to people, and people have been talking to us," he said. CIA has been talking to the top 10 players in the industry about where the industry is going, he said.
